story.title: Two waltzes a year
story.lede: Punjab grows wheat through the winter and rice through the monsoon. Every field loops across the floor twice, and you can read the farm calendar from the loops.
body: A growing crop adds leaves and stems, so HV climbs pass after pass. At harvest the canopy is gone in a day and the dot drops back to bare soil. That loop is the waltz.

Rice starts differently. Farmers flood the paddies in June, and smooth water mirrors the radar away, so whole districts go dark. Once seedlings stand in the water, the pulse bounces off water and stems and HH jumps. Then the waltz begins again.

beats.caption: Wheat near its peak: the fields crowd into the crops zone.
Wheat harvest. The canopy is gone and the dots fall back to bare soil.
Paddies flood: the fields go dark.
Rice at full height, the second waltz of the year.
Rice harvest. The floor empties again, ready for wheat.
